title: Present Perfect, Past Simple and Past Perfect

questions.instruction: Choose the best answer.

promptSegments.text: This is the first time I ___ this game.

feedback.explanation: “This is the first time” describes an experience up to the present.

questions.instruction: Replace only the bold verb phrase.

feedback.explanation: “Yesterday” is a finished past time, so use the past simple.

questions.instruction: Choose the best answer.

promptSegments.text: The train left at 9:00. We arrived at 9:10. By the time we arrived, the train ___.

feedback.explanation: The departure was completed before our arrival. It was not still happening when we arrived.

questions.instruction: Your task is still unfinished now. Start with “I”. Use every token exactly once.

promptSegments.text: Your task is still unfinished now.

feedback.explanation: The present perfect with “not … yet” describes something not completed up to now.

questions.instruction: Replace only the bold verb phrase.

feedback.explanation: “Since Monday” connects the past to now. Use have + past participle; see → seen.

questions.instruction: Choose the best answer.

promptSegments.text: At the school concert last Friday, Ben ___ a song.

feedback.explanation: “Last Friday” places the event at a finished past time.

questions.instruction: Replace only the bold verb phrase.

promptSegments.text: By the time the taxi arrived, we

feedback.explanation: The bags were taken outside before the taxi arrived. Use had + taken.

questions.instruction: Choose the best answer.

promptSegments.text: Nora moved here in 2020 and still lives here. She ___ here since 2020.

feedback.explanation: The situation began in the past and continues now.

questions.instruction: Ask your friend about yesterday’s football game. Start with “Where”. Use every token exactly once.

promptSegments.text: Ask your friend about yesterday’s football game.

feedback.explanation: A past-simple question uses did + subject + base verb.

questions.instruction: Replace only the bold verb phrase.

feedback.explanation: “So far today” means up to now. The singular subject Sam takes has.

questions.instruction: Choose the best answer.

promptSegments.text: I wasn’t hungry when lunch was served. I ___ a big breakfast two hours earlier.

feedback.explanation: Breakfast happened before the past moment when lunch was served.

questions.instruction: Replace only the bold verb phrase.

feedback.explanation: The event happened at a finished past time. Go → went.

questions.instruction: Choose the best answer.

promptSegments.text: We started this worksheet ten minutes ago and are still working on it. So far, we ___ only two questions.

feedback.explanation: “So far” reports progress up to the present moment.

questions.instruction: Nina ate dinner at 6:30. I arrived at 7:00. Start with “She”. Use the past perfect for the earlier action and every token exactly once.

promptSegments.text: Nina ate dinner at 6:30. I arrived at 7:00.

questions.canonicalAnswer: She had eaten dinner when I arrived.
acceptedVariants: She had eaten dinner when I arrived.

feedback.explanation: Had eaten identifies the action completed before my arrival.

questions.instruction: Replace only the bold verb phrase.

feedback.explanation: This is a completed past event. Use saw, not the past participle seen.

questions.instruction: Choose the best answer.

promptSegments.text: When I was six, I ___ my first bike.

feedback.explanation: “When I was six” refers to a finished past period.

questions.instruction: Replace only the bold verb phrase.

promptSegments.text: Dinner finished at 7:30. We arrived at 8:00. By the time we arrived, everyone

feedback.explanation: Change has to had because the completed eating is earlier than another past event.

questions.instruction: Choose the best answer.

promptSegments.text: The school term is still in progress. Since it began, there ___ three class trips.

feedback.explanation: The period extends to now, and the plural “three class trips” takes have.

questions.instruction: Replace only the bold verb phrase.

promptSegments.text: these glasses since June, and she still wears them every day.

feedback.explanation: Her possession began in June and continues now. The present perfect of have is has had.

questions.instruction: We first met Alex last Friday. Describe the time before that meeting. Start with “We”. Use every token exactly once.

promptSegments.text: We first met Alex last Friday. Describe the time before that meeting.

feedback.explanation: The past perfect looks back from last Friday to the time before our first meeting.
